items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...And he's the one that played it, but not La Raffin. [INTERVIEWEE] I'm different, putting a name from meatball, plurine, keep a shuffling and all that sort of stuff. I don't know how they can get the liars.

ctx.x: Of course, he began to improve a considerable lot. Yeah. But when I'd take him in the parades, I'd pay him as well as I paid the rest of the men. So he couldn't play much then? Well, he couldn't play very much, no. In fact, whether he didn't know how to play these numbers or not, I don't know. But eventually he did. He got onto all of that stuff, you see. Then he began to play the connet pretty good. He played a pretty good trumpet.

That's another liar. That he... That Tiger Rag. He's another liar. He didn't write Tiger Rag. No, he didn't. No, not half of it, no. Because he played... And Alcide Nunes, they used to call it plurine and meatballs, the same thing. And he's the one that played it, but not La Raffin.

I'm different, putting a name from meatball, plurine, keep a shuffling and all that sort of stuff. I don't know how they can get the liars. But you can bet all he writes and all he has written and all he has said.
